result.commit: 2d665e2 "WP2: the DailyFeature leaf, its parse branch, and the (S,D) field resolver"
deviations: Design's WP2 test table names cs_bucket_rank(day_max(Ret), FloatCap) as an example; cs_bucket_rank (and cs_winsor) is a Partura-plugin-only ND kernel (ops_ext.py's NEW_OPERATORS) and does not exist in AlphaCube's own default_registry() -- confirmed by direct lookup. Substituted cs_regres, the only ND-face arity-2 non-boolean operator AlphaCube ships, which exercises the identical type-system behavior (an ND op fed one day_*-reduced operand and one bare DailyFeature operand). Noted in the new test file's own module docstring too.

_require_board_rule's 'at least one STAR/GEM/BSE prefix must fire' guard (must_fix #2) is applied to BOTH LimitWidth and BoardCode, not just LimitWidth. The design's text states the MUST-raise requirement specifically for LimitWidth; BoardCode shares the same helper and therefore the same guard, since an undetected all-MAIN BoardCode on a format-mismatched symbol list is exactly the other half of the identical silent-failure mode the design's Overview/Risks sections describe for LimitWidth. No file outside the WP2 list was touched for this -- it is an in-scope behavior choice inside dailyfields.py.

Measured (not just read) that the design's specific precision claim for logging before the float32 cast does not hold at the stated 1e9-1e13 cap / ~1e-3 move regime: using the real nd_ts.ts_delta kernel, swept over cap in {1e9, 1e12, 1e13} and move in {1e-2 .. 1e-8}, ts_delta(FloatCap,1) recovered the true move with LOWER relative error than ts_delta(LogFloatCap,1) in every single case tried, typically by a factor of roughly log(cap) (~20-40x) -- the opposite of 'ts_delta(LogFloatCap,1) ... does not have this problem.' The log-before-cast STEP itself is kept exactly as the design's code skeleton specifies (it is harmless -- at this magnitude it is numerically identical to logging after the cast -- and not computationally expensive), but dailyfields.py's module docstring and resolve()'s docstring were written to state this measured finding plainly instead of repeating the now-falsified justification as fact. WP3's own test-plan line ('ts_delta(LogFloatCap,1) ... recovers a 1e-3 day-over-day move to better than 1e-5 relative, while ts_delta(FloatCap,1) does not') will not hold if implemented literally -- its author should re-derive or drop that comparison rather than assume it will pass.

BoardCode's numeric encoding (BOARD_MAIN=0.0, BOARD_STAR=1.0, BOARD_GEM=2.0, BOARD_BSE=3.0) is not pinned anywhere in the design text, which only says 'from the symbol's numeric prefix, using the same prefix extraction.' I invented this 4-category mapping and exported the four named constants from dailyfields.py so no downstream caller has to hardcode the numbers; WP3/WP9 (and any research code) consuming BoardCode should treat this encoding as dailyfields.py's own convention, open to revision.
result.notes:
New public names this package adds (for the reviewer and for WP3/WP4/WP9 implementers building on top):

- expression.DailyFeature(field): a new Expression subclass, __slots__=("field",), key f"DF:{field}", shape is COLLAPSED (the module singleton, by identity), _repr is just the field name. Added to expression.__all__.
- expression.operand_ok gained one isinstance(operand, DailyFeature) check inside the needs_full_m branch (before the degenerate tests), returning False unconditionally (both strict and legacy) -- a bare daily leaf fed to day_*/in_*/nt_* is rejected either way. _why_not got a matching clause. is_valid_root's isinstance tuple is now (Feature, DailyFeature).
- dailyfields.py (new module, zero imports from store.py/engine/): STORED_FIELDS, DERIVED_FIELDS, LOG_OF, LIST_AGE_SENTINEL=10000.0, DERIVED_VERSION=1, BOARD_MAIN/BOARD_STAR/BOARD_GEM/BOARD_BSE; derive(name, symbols, dates, *, tradable=None, status=None) -> (S,D) float64; class DailyFieldStore(root) with .fields/.symbols/.dates/.meta_sha256/.plane(name)/.align(name, symbols, dates); resolve(name, symbols, dates, *, store=None, tradable=None, status=None) -> (S,D) float32; available(store=None) -> Tuple[str,...]; fingerprint(store) -> Optional[str].
- parser.DAILY_FIELD_ALIASES (new, exported). parser._Parser's local boolean flag was renamed self.daily_fields -> self.coerce_bare_fields at all six sites (it is private/unexported, but anyone grepping the old name across sessions should know it moved). name() now checks the daily-leaf namespace LAST and never consults coerce_bare_fields for it.

Design choices I made where the text did not fully specify behavior (flagging so a reviewer can check I guessed right):
- ListAge's _lifecycle_mask priority: status (preferred -- TRADING/RESUMED/SUSPENDED all count as in-lifecycle, only OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE=0 does not) over tradable (fallback -- TRADING/RESUMED only, so a stock suspended on its very first in-lifecycle day would misread as not-yet-listed that one day) over neither given (defaults every requested day to in-lifecycle, so every symbol gets the sentinel). Matches store.py's DAY_STATUS_CODES convention (0=OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE) by value, duplicated rather than imported per the module's own no-store.py-import rule.
- parser.name()'s alias path re-validates the DAILY_FIELD_ALIASES-resolved name against self.reg.daily_fields (not just against the alias table's value set) before accepting it -- stricter than the pre-existing FIELD_ALIASES path, which trusts its alias table unconditionally. Deliberate: Registry.daily_fields can legitimately be a proper subset of the canonical 9 (WP1's own tests/test_catalog.py already exercises build_registry(daily_fields=("FloatCap",))), and this keeps that restriction airtight through an alias too, mirroring how registry_name() already re-validates operator aliases against the live registry.
- I did not build a full synthetic-store-backed ListAge test (unlisted_days=8 against a real CubeStore/CubeView) -- that fixture (and the symbol-spelling fix board_limit needs) is explicitly WP3's file (synthetic.py/conftest.py). WP2's own ListAge tests use small hand-built (symbols, dates, status) arrays directly against dailyfields.derive(), which is what WP2's test-plan line ("derive() for all three derived fields against hand-computed arrays") asks for.
- Ran the task's required commands exactly: focused set (tests/test_expression.py tests/test_parser.py tests/test_general_call.py tests/test_legacy_corpus.py tests/test_catalog.py tests/test_mining.py tests/test_tokens_env.py tests/test_engine.py) all green before the full run; full `pytest tests/ -q` is 705 passed / 10 skipped / 1 xfailed, i.e. exactly 639 (WP6-fix baseline) + 66 (this package's new tests), confirming no existing test's outcome changed.
